title: From Stone to Food: Foodways and Ground Stone Tools During the Natufian and Early Neolithic of Eastern Jordan
lineage: Publisher full text hosted on ResearchGate. Its artefact analysis uses different archaeological objects from the 2018 bread-fragment study with partly overlapping authors.

passages.locator: Section 3.1, Shubayqa Sites, Setting and Dating
passages.note: The Early Natufian phases 4–7 span approximately 14,800–14,100 cal BP at 68.2% using IntCal20.

passages.locator: Section 4.1, Early Natufian Use-Wear, table 2 and fig. 4
passages.note: In Early Natufian Shubayqa 1, wear on a handstone suggests seed or cereal grinding. Wear on a combined quern and mortar and nearby tool is consistent with grinding or pounding tubers or similar soft plants. The excavators compare these traces with food remains of the same broad period.

passages.locator: End of section 3, immediately before GST Use-Wear Results
passages.note: The authors flag the small early sample and ambiguity of use-wear interpretations.
